note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Adult with a few-days history of widespread, worsening itchy, dry eczema involving chest, hands/arms and antecubital fossae; plan to start antihistamine and a stronger topical steroid.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Several-day history of sore, red, very itchy, dry skin, worse over the past few days.
- Distribution/onset/progression: Involved chest, hands, arms, especially inside of the elbows (antecubital areas); onset over past few days, progressive/worse recently.
- Skin characteristics: Very itchy and dry; some areas are cracked; no weeping/clear discharge; no visible scratch marks reported; patient does not report thickened or darkened skin.
- Prior similar episodes: History of eczema; patient reports prior treatments have not recently controlled this flare.
- Treatments/current self-care:
  - Uses Diprobase (emollient) — continued.
  - Uses a product called "dermal" in the shower — continued.
  - Has used over-the-counter hydrocortisone previously — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Tried an over-the-counter antihistamine previously (patient later referenced cetirizine but statements about antihistamine use are inconsistent) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Pertinent negatives: No fever reported, no joint pains reported. No weeping of lesions.
- Past medical history: Eczema, asthma (uses blue inhaler PRN).
- Allergies: Patient states no known drug allergies.
- Family history/social/preventive: Mother with hypothyroidism and migraine. Patient located in London. No other social history documented.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Skin exam findings (patient-reported): Red, sore, dry, itchy patches on chest, hands, arms, worst in inside of elbows; cracked areas; no weeping, no obvious scratch marks, no reported lichenification/darkening.

Impression:
- Widespread eczema flare/exacerbation.

Plan:
- Prescriptions:
  - Fexofenadine prescribed for symptomatic control of itch/urticaria — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Betnovate topical (brand named) to treat eczema flare; patient instructed to apply a very small amount (approx. fingertip unit) twice daily for the next couple of weeks; dose/route not fully documented (topical route implied; strength not documented).
- Continue regular emollient therapy (Diprobase) and shower product ("dermal") as before.
- Pharmacy: Prescription to be sent to Boots for collection.
- Safety/follow-up:
  - Advise to return or contact earlier if no improvement or if condition worsens or if any adverse/allergic reaction occurs.
  - Routine review suggested at ~2 weeks if no improvement.

document_quality / Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs and clinician-performed skin examination details (extent, morphology, secondary infection signs).
  - Photographs of lesions or dermatology review if atypical.
  - Exact medication doses, strengths, routes and duration for prescribed drugs (Fexofenadine, Betnovate).
  - Detailed medication reconciliation (current inhaler name/dose, steroid past-use details).
  - Pregnancy status in female patients (not asked/documented).
  - Contact details/next appointment date.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Antihistamine use: patient initially stated no current antihistamines, later stated they had tried OTC antihistamines and they did not work.
  - Steroid use: some ambiguity whether patient is currently using hydrocortisone or only used it previously and whether it helped ("tried" vs "still using"); conflict noted.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Overall understandable but contains short pauses, some fragmented or overlapping speech and a few inaudible fragments; occasional clinician–patient statement confusion.
